A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rinse process could be used to fabricate a flexible and thin BTESE organosilica nanolayer on a commercial polymeric support with high permeance and high selectivity for the dehydration of IPA/waters mixtures via VP.
the FD method is an excellent approach for the fabrication of thin organosilicas on porous polymeric membranes with high permeance and flexibility.

the rinse process could be used to fabricate an organosilica thin film on a porous polymeric support, which could lead to a flexible and thin composite organosilica/polymer membrane with high permeability and selectivity for dehydration of IPA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a thin organosilic membrane with high permeability can be fabricated on commercialized polymeric supports via a rinse strategy.
the rinsed membrane showed a high water permeance and separation factor for the VP dehydration of IPA/wate

a flexible organosilica layer with a high permeance can be obtained via the FD process with a rinsed strategy, which can be used as a promising separation membrane for dehydration of IPA in the VP and pervaporative process.
